subject: R feature request: log prob + grad

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: R feature request: log prob + grad
parts:
Dave Blei just made an excellent suggestion, which I just
added to our RStan to-do list:

* (RStan) Expose to R for a model:

-- log prob and gradient functions
-- inits -> unconstrained param transform
-- results -> constrained param transform

Then users could do all sorts of things just with our models,
like run optimizers, Metropolis, etc.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: R feature request: log prob + grad
parts:
You need to call

model.log_prob(...);

and pass non-constant vectors (they're not declared const,
which I've been meaning to fix, but it's all tangled up
with the io::reader class's mappings).

The R output stream looks right, but you might want to try it
with 0 just in case that's causing some kind of compilation problem
then add in the R stream later.

What's the error message?

- Bob

      std::vector<double> par_r = Rcpp::as<std::vector<double> >(params_r);

On Tuesday, February 26, 2013 2:28:42 PM UTC-5, Jiqiang Guo wrote:
A suggestion on grad_prob_log: I noticed that log_prob is also a byproduct of grad_prob_log. So would it be a good idea to return log_prob for this function as well say using a parameter?  I am thinking if I need prob_log and then grad_prob_log in R, it would be more efficient that if only grad_prob_log is called.

This would be a good idea. It wouldn't help much when calling optim() but it would help for nlm(), which allows returning the gradient as an attribute of the function value.

Ben
